I could be mistaken, but I consider the two main use cases for icc to be:
1- You are developing software that you distribute as binary, and you offer an intel-optimized version compiled with icc.
2- You have written one or more programs for your own use that are highly CPU intensive, and you have an Intel chip so you use icc to get that extra performance.

I think the first case doesn't really matter which CPU you are running on, and the second case is more something you do if you have both the CPU intensive custom program(s) and an Intel chip already.

Basically, I wouldn't use icc as a reason to buy an Intel chip unless I was in group (2).
